meta.title: Flinder
meta.description: Tinder for flies. A real 166,700-neuron fly brain, running in your browser, swipes through dating profiles: its pC1 mating-drive neurons decide left or right. It's a match when the other fly's brain swipes right too.

head.title: Flinder
head.sub: Tinder for flies. A real fly brain swipes through dating profiles and its mating-drive neurons say left or right. If the other fly's brain swipes right too, it's a match.

swiper.title: The swiper
swiper.note: Its own profile is what the other flies' brains judge. Send the link and a friend runs this same fly. Beat its score.

meter.title: Inside its head
meter.note: Spikes from the fly's real 166,700-neuron connectome, running in your browser. It smells each profile (cVA, Or47b, vinegar), sees it (LC10a) and hears it (Johnston's organ). Past the first line it swipes right, past the second it's a super like. In a chat each message is sensed the same way: pC1 flirts back, a fly coming on too strong trips the giant fibre and it bails, and a bored brain grooms its antennae.
